S0872.L3t: Wien's displacement law states that the peak wavelength is inversely proportional to temperature, so a body at 300 K (20 times cooler than the Sun) will have a peak wavelength 20 times longer than the Sun's 500 nm.
S0872.L3f: A common mistake is to think that the peak wavelength scales directly with temperature, so a cooler body would have a shorter peak wavelength, leading to a value much smaller than 500 nm.
